title: Remember
author: Christina Rossetti
text:
Remember me when I am gone away,
Gone far away into the silent land;
When you can no more hold me by the hand,
Nor I half turn to go yet turning stay.
Remember me when no more day by day
You tell me of our future that you planned:
Only remember me; you understand
It will be late to counsel then or pray.
Yet if you should forget me for a while
And afterwards remember, do not grieve:
For if the darkness and corruption leave
A vestige of the thoughts that once I had,
Better by far you should forget and smile
Than that you should remember and be sad.
who: Christina Georgina Rossetti (5 December 1830 to 29 December 1894) was an English poet, born in London, the youngest of four children and the younger sister of the artist and poet Dante Gabriel Rossetti. Goblin Market and Other Poems, published by Macmillan in 1862 when she was 31, was her first commercially printed collection and the book in which this sonnet first appeared.
why: The poem was first published in 1862 in Goblin Market and Other Poems. There is no documented account, in the pages consulted, of the occasion that prompted it or of the person it addresses, so it is best read as a speaker's request rather than as a record of one event.
notice: Notice how the first eight lines ask to be remembered and the last six take the request back. Watch the turn at the word "Yet", where the tone shifts from plea to permission. Notice what the final line puts above remembrance.
prompts: Is there someone whose happiness you would put before being remembered by them?
What would you want the people you love to do with the memory of you: keep it, or set it down lightly?
